heme_involvement_pattern.staging_system: Phases: chronic phase, accelerated phase, blast phase (>=20% blasts, resembles acute leukaemia). Risk scores: Sokal, EUTOS, ELTS.

biomarkers.name: BCR-ABL1 t(9;22)
biomarkers.prevalence: >95% (defining; rare cryptic/variant rearrangements detectable by FISH/PCR)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Diagnosis by cytogenetics/FISH/PCR. Standardised RQ-PCR (International Scale — IS) for monitoring response. Response milestones: BCR-ABL1 <=10% at 3 months, <=1% at 6 months, <=0.1% (MMR) by 12 months. Treatment-free remission possible in sustained deep molecular response (typically MR4 or MR4.5, depending on protocol)

biomarkers.name: p210 vs p190 vs p230 transcript
biomarkers.prevalence: p210 (e13a2, e14a2) ~95% of CML; p190 rare; p230 very rare
biomarkers.clinical_use: Helps distinguish typical CML from rarer BCR-ABL1-positive myeloid neoplasms and from Ph+ ALL, in which p190 is more common

biomarkers.name: ABL kinase domain mutations
biomarkers.clinical_use: Guide TKI selection at resistance. T315I: ponatinib or asciminib. F317L/V/I/C and V299L: nilotinib preferred over dasatinib. Y253H, E255K/V, F359V/C/I: dasatinib preferred over nilotinib

biomarkers.name: Additional cytogenetic abnormalities (ACAs)
biomarkers.prevalence: Can emerge during progression; more common in accelerated / blast phase
biomarkers.clinical_use: Adverse; especially major-route abnormalities such as +8, an additional Ph, i(17q), +19; complex abnormalities and certain lesions including -7/7q- are also adverse

biomarkers.name: Sokal, EUTOS, ELTS risk scores
biomarkers.clinical_use: ELTS is commonly preferred for TKI-era survival prediction. Sokal: age, spleen, platelet, blasts. ELTS: age, spleen size, platelet count, peripheral blood blasts

biomarkers.name: Asciminib response (STAMP allosteric inhibitor)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Approved for chronic phase CML resistant/intolerant to >=2 prior TKIs; also approved/active in T315I

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Chronic phase: marrow granulocytic hyperplasia with left-shifted maturation (all stages of myeloid maturation present), often with basophilia and eosinophilia; splenic red pulp expansion
variants: accelerated phase (criteria vary by classification; may include 10-19% blasts, increased basophils, thrombocytopenia/thrombocytosis unresponsive to therapy, or clonal evolution)
blast phase (>=20% blasts — myeloid ~70% or lymphoid ~20-30%)
histomorphological_subtype.grading: Not graded; phase is the key stratification

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Interferon-α historically effective — some patients achieve treatment-free remission through immune surveillance of residual disease
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Marrow hypercellularity; splenic red pulp expansion

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Haematopoietic stem cell (HSC) with BCR-ABL1 fusion — same fusion in CML causes multilineage clonality (myeloid, erythroid, megakaryocytic, and sometimes lymphoid involvement, especially in blast crisis)
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Chronic phase: preserved granulocytic maturation with left shift; blast crisis represents loss of maturation with maturation arrest (myeloid ~70% or lymphoid ~20-30%)
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: HSC-origin explains multilineage involvement (myeloid predominant but affecting multiple haematopoietic lineages); blast crisis represents progressive dedifferentiation with additional genetic events (for example TP53, RUNX1, IKZF1 alterations); can transform to either myeloid or lymphoid blast crisis reflecting HSC lineage potential
